podcast.body: Released on the Virgin Label on May 27, 1977. The song controversially connected the words "queen" and "moron." Virgin Records faced significant challenges pressing the record, as some workers at the manufacturing plant were so offended they refused to work. The BBC banned it, citing "gross bad taste" and a possible breach of the Broadcasting Act, effectively saying the song broke the law. Most radio and TV stations even refused to broadcast commercials for it, and major chain stores like Woolworths and Boots banned its sale. Despite all obstacles, it sold 150,000 copies in just five days, but was denied the number one spot on the official record charts due to alleged rigging, being listed as number two. The chart publishers further showed their disapproval by leaving a blank space where the band's name should have been printed at number two. "The Sex Pistols with God Save the Queen released on the Virgin Label on May 27th, 1977."
